title: Prototypes of Actin Arrangement in the Focal Adhesion (FA) of Cultured Respiratory Tract Epithelial Cells
content: The adhesive contacts that a cell makes with the extracellular matrix are characterized by an organized array of actin filaments at the cytoplasmic surface. Although the canonical organization of such sites is believed to rely on integration of actin with integrin at the plasma membrane, the precise arrangement of filaments in the FA has not been studied. As the adhesive strength of FAs is less in cancer cells than in normal cells, it is important to analyze their organization. The sites can be visualized by acquiring series of tilt images in Thermo Talos L120C and reconstructing them in Inspect3D software. Cells were subcultured on Permanox® (Nalge Nunc International, NY) dishes that had been coated with platinum in a Denton BTT-IV high vacuum coater as described elsewhere [1]. After rinsing briefly with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline, the cells were permeabilized with 50µg/ml of digitonin in cytoskeletal buffer (150 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 5 mM ethylene glycol-bis(2-aminoethyl ether)-N,N,N (EGTA), 5 mM 135 glucose, 10 mM 2-(N-morpholino)ethane sulfonic acid (MES); pH 7) along with 10 µM /ml of phalloidin to stabilize the filaments. The dishes were incubated for 2 hours with occasional swirling, then rinsed again before being fixed with 2% paraformaldehyde, 2.5% glutaraldehyde, 0.05% tannic acid, 0.1 M cacodylate buffer, 10% w/v sucrose. A conventional protocol for resin embedding in Spurr’s resin was followed, and pieces of the polymerized resin were cut and glued onto blocks for thin sectioning. Sections were stained with uranyl acetate and lead citrate, then screened in a Zeiss EM10 transmission electron microscope to identify FAs. These areas were then imaged in the Talos 120.
